document_title: Six Data Center Sites. Two Answer to Juneau.
post_copy:
From the North Slope to Cook Inlet, six sites could host data centers, and Alaska's next governor could reach two.

At Milepost 390, DNR's preliminary decision describes a 1 to 3 GW gas plant that feeds its computers and no Alaska grid. Near Houston, a DNR notice proposes conveying about 19,950 acres to AIDEA. Neither decision is final. The governor appoints DNR's commissioner.

The rest are federal. Air Force proposals for JBER, Eielson and Clear closed June 29th with no award. FERC takes Cook Inlet permit filings until November 2nd. Alaska votes November 3rd. The winner can veto any data center bill.

The maps ink the two state sites in gold and ring the four federal ones in dashes. All four candidates are quoted at equal size.

How much should data centers count in a vote for a governor who could reach two sites and holds a veto?

#AlaskaGovernor #AlaskaDataCenters #AlaskaDNR

slides.headline: Two sit on state land. Four are federal calls.
slides.body: The North Slope lease and the Houston land are decided in the Department of Natural Resources, whose commissioner the governor appoints. The Air Force decides three bases. FERC decides Cook Inlet's preliminary permit.

slides.kicker: THE FOUR CANDIDATES, IN THEIR OWN WORDS
slides.headline: What they say about data centers.
slides.body: "I'm a big believer in data centers." He said the groups he is talking to would produce their own power (Bronson, Republican, Commonwealth North forum). "I support a moratorium on data center development in Alaska until the Legislature can pass a comprehensive regulatory framework for that development in Alaska." (Kreiss-Tomkins, Democrat, September 8th forum). "I think we need to embrace it." Any data center, he said, must "bring their own energy." (Taylor, Republican, September 8th forum). "I will never allow Alaska to be littered with hyperscale data centers that take our resources and spoil our lands." (Wilson, Republican, by text message). Order is alphabetical by surname, not a ranking. Quotes as reported by the Alaska Beacon.

slides.headline: Milepost 390. State land, 50 years.
slides.body: DNR proposes a 50-year lease on 715.4 acres beside the Dalton Highway, 26 miles south of Deadhorse. Its final decision would be signed by the Division of Oil and Gas, under authority delegated from the DNR commissioner. The same decision says what powers it.

slides.kicker: FROM DNR'S PRELIMINARY DECISION ON THE LEASE
slides.headline: "not interconnected to the Railbelt or any other Alaska utility grid"
slides.body: A gas plant designed for 1 to 3 GW, all used on site. Two candidates raised the same point.

slides.headline: One state decision, three federal ones.
slides.body: DNR proposes giving AIDEA about 19,950 acres two miles north of Houston. No final decision appears on the notice. The Air Force offered to lease about 4,700 acres at JBER, Eielson and Clear, with no award yet.

slides.headline: Filings close the day before the vote.
slides.body: DeepGreen proposes a 100 MW subsea data center in Cook Inlet, and FERC decides its preliminary permit. The Kenai Peninsula Borough filed to intervene. The deadline is November 2nd.

slides.headline: Who signs each one.
slides.body: Preliminary decision. No final decision on the notice, for the North Slope lease (ADL 422741), which DNR signs under the commissioner's delegation. For a data center bill, the Legislature, then the governor. The Senate passed one 14 to 5. The House didn't pass it. A veto takes two-thirds to override. For JBER, Eielson and Clear, the Department of the Air Force. Proposals closed June 29th. No award. For the Houston land to AIDEA, DNR. No final decision on the notice. For Cook Inlet (P-15423-000), FERC. Filings close November 2nd.

Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes, with a source link wherever a fact is disputed.
